text="В зимний месяц 2022 года, на снег опять окутанном, президент Российской Федерации Владимир Путин предложил правительству использовать средства Фонда национального благосостояния (ФНБ) в качестве топлива для распилающегося полета транспорта небесного и водного. text="Aiming for financial freedom, many pile their savings into banks in pursuit of interest on investments. However, experts caution: the accumulated capital gradually diminishes due to tax deductions and inflation. It seems reasonable to abandon work and move a substantial sum to deposit, but specialists at Sberbank and T-Bank show that to maintain an average national income level, one needs a deposit ranging from 13 to 18.9 million rubles depending on the specific investment conditions. People are prone to view bank deposits as a reliable shield against economic risks, yet this belief is misguided. In reality, such investments can lead to the loss of real value of accumulated capital: without regular investment, the size of earnings remains stagnant. The main issue with Russian rentiers lies not so much in the interest rate, but rather its ratio with inflation. According to experts, spending all earned income results in a gradual decrease in purchasing power. For instance, at a 10% annual interest rate and an inflation rate of 5%, real yield will be only 5%, while spending all earnings annually will result in a 5% loss of savings every year. Over ten years, such a strategy would double the cost of purchased goods, turning the dream of comfortable living into a path to a lower standard of living. Beyond inflation, there are additional obstacles for capital preservation: tax payments and the risk of losing a bank license. As of 2026, incomes from deposits below 160,000 rubles will not be taxed, while the rest will be subject to tax at a rate of 13–15%. The scope of deposit insurance covers a maximum of 1.4 million rubles, making the placement of large sums less secure. To safeguard large capitals, it's necessary to distribute funds among multiple financial institutions, which complicates financial management. Therefore, specialists recommend considering various investment instruments besides bank deposits: bonds, real estate, securities, taking into account current market conditions." ratio=42.6
